why: The #946 ban stops telling a runtime edge from a type-only one: the skip inverts, so `import type { X } from './dev-x'` is reported as pulling the developer module into the bundle and a real value import is not. This is the distinction the whole ban rests on: a developer chunk is splittable only if nothing on an ordinary path imports it for VALUE, while hud.ts, loop.ts, route-ui.ts, route-host.ts and bench.ts all name developer modules through leading `import type`s. Under the mutation the sweep reports those, the plain-value fixture is reported clean and the leading-import-type fixture is reported, which is why the three named tests fail. `every developer module named in the list still exists` passes either way, as it must: it reads the list, not the classifier. Re-anchored for #1016, which replaced the pinned inventory and its own regex with the ban's use of the layer scan's extractor.
